reason: Post-anthesis LAI is short across every grain-filling bin (-0.56, -0.52, -0.38, -0.19) while the pre-anthesis bins are fine or high; senescence starts too early. (Retry of iteration 1, which failed on a stale-filesystem read, not on the parameters.)
hypothesis: Temperature-driven leaf death begins at DVSDLT=1.2, just after the peak. Delaying it to 1.4 should lift LAI through DVS 1.0-1.5, lengthen the plateau (sim 44d vs obs 56d) and raise the matched peak (sim 3.29 vs obs 3.75) without touching the early canopy.
reasoning: Three shape features fail together and all sit after the peak: peak level -0.56, plateau duration -8 days, and a monotonically shrinking negative bias from DVS 1.0 to 2.0. A single senescence-onset parameter explains all three; an SLA change would need four separate nodes to do the same and would also perturb the pre-anthesis bins that are currently unbiased (-0.02 at DVS 0.5-1.0). Ruled out RDRLeavesTableRelativeRate because the observed decline rate (-0.039/day) is already matched by the simulated one (-0.034/day) - the rate is right, the onset is early. Ruled out LAICR/RDRSHM because they lower the peak rather than raise it. The early-season overshoot (+0.34 at DVS<0.25) is a separate issue for a later iteration, where TDWI or RGRLAI is the lever.
expected_effect: DVS-binned RMSE down from 0.786; biases in bins 1.0-1.75 move toward zero; plateau duration closer to 56 days; early bins unchanged.
